subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 new third-party action revisions in workflows that use secrets, tokens, publishing credentials, and security-scanning permissions?
rationale: SHA pinning prevents tag drift but does not establish trust in newly pinned executable code, and exact-head CI cannot decide whether the privileged upstream changes fit OpenClaw's security policy.

options.title: Accept after refresh
options.body: Rebase onto current main, require exact-head checks, inspect the upstream revision ranges, and merge if the privileged changes are acceptable.

options.title: Split privileged revisions
options.body: Separate token, publishing, scanning, and Codex-agent action updates from lower-risk setup-tool updates for narrower review.

options.title: Retain current pins
options.body: Pause or close the batch if the privileged upstream changes cannot be reviewed with sufficient confidence.

recommendation.title: Accept after refresh
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main, require exact-head checks, inspect the upstream revision ranges, and merge if the privileged changes are acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history shows the strongest ownership across CI, Docker release, action-runtime modernization, and Codex-driven agent workflows.
